title: Efficient Layer-wise LLM Fine-tuning for Revision Intention Prediction
key_contributions: Introduces IR-Tuning: layer-wise PEFT that dynamically selects important LLM layers
Addresses the problem: predicting nuanced revision intentions (coherence, clarity, style, grammar) from before/after text pairs
Shows LLMs pre-trained for generation struggle at classification tasks
Demonstrates parameter-efficient fine-tuning works well on small, specialized revision corpora
Outperforms QLoRA and other layer-wise PEFT baselines on ITERATER corpus

problem_formulation.challenge: Given two versions of text, predict the writer's intention behind the revision (not just what changed, but why)
problem_formulation.example: Original: 'We also leverage the image features to incorporate the style information of words in LayoutLM.' Revised (Clarity): 'We also leverage the image features to incorporate the visual information of words in LayoutLM.' (changed 'style' to 'visual')
problem_formulation.difficulty: Same surface pattern can represent different intentions; requires understanding context and purpose

direct_implication_for_skill: Change classification (what type changed) is easier than intent prediction (why it changed). The skill's 'worked_example' and 'resolution_requirement' fields attempt to capture intent; this paper shows fine-grained intent prediction benefits from careful model tuning, not just prompting.
potential_application: If skill needs to distinguish between 'field renamed' (same intent) vs. 'semantic shift' (new intent), could adapt IR-Tuning approach for task-specific fine-tuning on small revision corpora.
reading_notes: Important for understanding the distinction between 'what changed' (easier) vs. 'why it changed' (harder). Section 1 clearly frames the problem. Not directly applicable now, but valuable reference for future skill iterations on intent classification.
